## Active

### D-081 — kukum lives in a dispatch orchestrator to keep filesystem access narrow

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

The `blong-kukum` capability needs filesystem and registry access, which only port factories get, so
the replica of the `[REUSE_SERVER]` pattern could not stay in an adapter. The choice was
`orchestrator.dispatch` with `namespace: 'kukum'` (registering `ports.kukum.request`) over either an
adapter or adding `platform`/`fs` to `IHandlerProxy`. The latter would have exposed filesystem
writes to every handler in the framework; the orchestrator keeps the blast radius to one layer.
Reconsider if kukum ever needs to be loaded without blong-server.

### D-082 — kukum's API surface is generated from its primitive catalogue

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

One `validation` export emits the roughly 70 dotted-triple keys and one `handler` export emits the
matching object map, with `layerProxy` normalizing both. This is the `subject.validation` plus
`blong-mock.validation(models)` pattern rather than a method-by-method hand-written surface. The
consequence is that adding a primitive to `core/blong-kukum/primitives/catalog.ts` adds five routes
with no new files, but the functions must carry an explicit `.name`.

### D-083 — kukum's routes are explicitly unauthenticated

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

kukum mutates source files on the local filesystem and is loaded alongside a dev suite, so requiring
a JWT would make it unusable; its own `index.ts` intentionally has no login or access realm, which
is also why the API needs no database. This mirrors `systemDebug` and `RestFs` being dev-oriented.
Reconsider if kukum is ever enabled in a shared or production environment: it then needs the same
`enabled` config gate as `systemDebug`.

### D-084 — kukum ships its own CLI binary instead of a blong-dev subcommand

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

`blong-dev` cannot depend on `blong-kukum`, because `blong-kukum` already devDepends on `blong-dev`
for its `ci-lint` and `ci-test` scripts, so Rush would see a project cycle. Shipping the bin with
the realm also means it works for anyone who installs the realm, without the dev toolchain.
Reconsider if the repo ever gains a tool package that may depend on realms.

### D-085 — The MCP surface is stateful, one transport per session id

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

The protocol requires `initialize` to precede other methods on the same session `Mcp-Session-Id`,
and the stateless per-request pattern answers every follow-up with `Method not found`. Tools are
derived from the gateway's route table through `IGateway.describe()` so the MCP surface cannot drift
from the API, and the item is off by default: kukum's own suite turns it on in `dev`, so the blast
radius is one suite.

### D-086 — kukum's realm primitive copies the blong-kopi template

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

Rather than the descriptor's minimal four files, `realm` scaffolding delegates to the `blong-kopi`
template, read through the host (`../blong-kopi` resolved from `operations.ts`). The realm must not
import `blong-gogo` (the runtime), and `createRealm` lives there, so the template is copied by the
engine. Consequence: the `realm` primitive inherits the template's naming constraint (a single
lowercase word) and the CLI works only where the sibling package exists.

### D-088 — kukum writes compose by default and --replace is the escape hatch

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

A second file under `meta/type/` is additive: the framework keys declared schemas as
`schema[<realm>][<object>]` and `layerProxy` merges each `meta/type/*.ts` into
`{[<realm>]: <that file>}`, proven by
`test/blong-int-adapter/mysql/meta/type/{schema.ts, schemaPage.ts}` whose test asserts both entities
land in `objectSchema`. That unblocked real merging: `schema`/`table` writes a sibling
`meta/type/<object>.ts`, `schema`/`register` splices into the existing `tables` map, `test` appends
its group to `integration.watch.test`, and `playwright` appends a `test.describe` block. Marker
detection was chosen over a flag because the marker is the same signal that already decides
hand-written versus generated: a file without it is never rewritten. `mode: 'replace'` maps to the
old regenerate-from-scratch behavior and keeps the lossy-file warning, so that warning is now
accurate rather than a permanent caveat. This supersedes the warning-only decision.

### D-089 — Merge is a per-descriptor compose hook, not a generic diff

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

`files(ctx)` still answers "what would this look like in an empty realm" and is used by `get`, while
`compose({host, root, context})` may read disk to return a non-destructive result. Text merging
lives in four narrow pure helpers in `merge.ts` (`appendStringEntry`, `insertMapEntry`,
`appendYamlBlock`, `appendDescribeBlock`), each recognizing one shape a template emits and returning
`undefined` when it does not, so the caller falls back to overwrite plus warning instead of
corrupting the file.

### D-090 — Seed artifacts are per entity, so they never needed merge support

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

The template writes `meta/db/<subject><Object>Merge.yaml` — one file per entity — so the original
`SHARED_FILES` concern for seeds was unfounded.

### D-091 — Generated test groups are registered, not merely described

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

A group missing from `integration.watch.test` silently never executes, and
`discoverRealmTestMethods` only auto-fills that list when a realm is loaded standalone (not as part
of a suite, and never for the browser side). So `test`/`server` and `test`/`browser` now edit
`index.ts` and `browser-test.ts` as part of generating the group; when that bootstrap is missing or
hand-written the result carries a `messages` entry naming the entry to add by hand. A new `notices`
channel on `PrimitiveFile` was chosen over failing the add, because the group file itself is still
useful.

### D-092 — Generated test bodies create a row and assert it comes back

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

`assert.ok(true, 'placeholder')` made "covered by its tests" meaningless, so the server and browser
groups now add a row through the generated handler and assert that `find` returns it. The Playwright
spec drives the generated model page through the shared `browseModel`, `createAndEditModel` and
`cleanupModel` helpers.

### D-093 — The generated model spec carries a browse table and edit cards

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

A model with only `cards` renders no browse table, so the Playwright helpers could not drive it. The
generated spec now carries `nameField`, `schema.properties.<object>` with `filter`, `sort` and a
`columns` widget, `cards.browse` and `cards.edit` plus a `browser` toolbar, mirroring the
`blong-kopi` template. Its path was also aligned to `<subject><Object>Model.ts` with a lowercase
subject, as the template writes it, so regenerating replaces the scaffolded model instead of leaving
two models claiming one entity.

### D-095 — The fixture splits template output and API output across two entities

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

`widget` is pure template output and stays untouched as the working baseline, while the API's own
output is a second entity, `gadget`. Adding `gadget` to the template's `widget` would have meant two
tables claiming one entity and a model overwriting the template's.

### D-096 — The fixture covers only primitives its three legs can exercise

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

The added set is deliberately small: table, registry entry, test seed, model, and one test per
platform. Adding `adapter`, `storybook` or `component` would have produced artifacts that no test in
that realm could exercise, quietly making the coverage assertion vacuous.

### D-097 — A generated test seed also grants the entity's actions

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

`seed`/`test` now composes the realm's `accessAuthorizationMerge.yaml`, adding the entity's five
actions to the `<realm>Manage` capability. Without it the generated entity is scaffolded but
unusable: every call is denied through the gateway, which is exactly what the browser leg reported.

### D-104 — The hand-written marker applies to code files only

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

The generated marker is a TypeScript sentinel, so treating a `.yaml` or `.sql` artifact that lacks
it as hand-written made seeds and stored procedures permanently unrefreshable. Non-code artifacts
are now always regenerable, composition into them is still opt-in per descriptor (the RBAC seed),
and reading them uses a marker-free helper.

### D-105 — The kukum Playwright leg borrows Vite from blong-browser

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

The fixture is not a Rush project, so it has no `node_modules`: `blong`, `blong-watch` and
`playwright` come from blong-kukum's tree and Vite from blong-browser's, both only put on PATH for
these runs. Adding `vite` to blong-kukum's own devDependencies would be cleaner but needs a
`rush update`.

### D-106 — Baselines are refreshed by a script and never by the test

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

`node --run kukum:fixture:update` regenerates the fixture and runs with `--update-snapshots`; the
test itself only ever compares. The update script carries the committed PNGs across the regeneration
by hand, because deleting the tree would otherwise take them with it.

### D-107 — The fixture's generated files are ignored, only baselines are committed

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

`test/fixture/e2e-realm/**` is gitignored except `test/e2e.play.ts-snapshots/`, using the standard
nested-negation idiom, so `e2e.test.ts` regenerates the fixture in place on every run instead of
comparing against a committed copy. It is the committed screenshots that lock the generators: a
template change that alters the rendered page fails until `node --run kukum:fixture:update`
refreshes them. The earlier "generate into a scratch directory and compare byte for byte" assertion
is gone — with the generated files uncommitted it would have compared the generators against
themselves and asserted nothing. What was lost is template-drift detection for non-UI files; what
was gained is a much smaller diff, no generated TypeScript in the package's lint surface, and a
drift check that only fires on changes a human can review.

### D-108 — Generated tests filter by the created row's name, not by paging

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

Four options were weighed for the `find`-returns-nothing bug: raise `pageSize`, order by primary key
descending, reset the fixture database each run, or filter by the unique name the test just created.
The filter won because it is the only option that stays correct no matter how the table grows, and
it needs no database lifecycle change; `search` (ILIKE) was rejected as looser than the exact
`filterBy`. The template now returns the created name from the `add` step so the `find` step can
filter on it, and `filterBy` turned out to be accepted over HTTP too, not just for in-process
dispatch — the passing browser leg is the proof.

### D-109 — The fixture race stays open rather than fixed with glob tricks

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

Re-verifying that positional globs ignore `--exclude` (tap still lists the fixture test) confirmed
the analysis already recorded in the friction and decision documents: the options that would fix the
race — a dot-directory, a temporary-directory swap, or a `blong-dev test` change honoring tap config
— either do not fully close the window or have repo-wide blast radius. It is not re-opened without a
deliberate decision to change `blong-dev test`.

### D-110 — kukum keeps pure operation modules beside thin library bindings

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

It looks redundant but is deliberate: the pure `operations/*.ts` modules, which take `host` and
`registry` explicitly, are what keep the existing `operations.test.ts` and `engine.test.ts` passing
untouched, and the `library()` bindings are what make the realm read like a normal Blong realm
(handler to library to operation). The bindings are one line each and are tested by calling the
factory with a stub api and the result with a fake `this` — the only way to prove a binding is thin,
since a value captured in the factory would still pass an integration test.

### D-136 — A handler-group file name matches its endpoint path minus the namespace

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

The rule, described by the user as the generic one: the file name must match the API endpoint path
minus the namespace; a file handling more than one path may use a generic word for the segment that
differs, or skip that segment entirely; double duty must be avoided. Applied in
`core/blong-kukum/orchestrator/kukum/`: `kukum.primitive.find` is `primitiveFind.ts`, the
`kukum.activation.find`, `method.find` and `tree.find` group is `activationFind.ts`, `methodFind.ts`
and `treeFind.ts`, `kukum.source.get` and `source.check` are `sourceGet.ts` and `sourceCheck.ts`,
and the 14 primitives that share `kukum.<id>.add/edit/find/get/check` use bare `add.ts`, `edit.ts`,
`find.ts`, `get.ts` and `check.ts`. The per-primitive files skip the differing segment rather than
using `primitive` as the generic word, because `kukum.primitive.find` is a real endpoint, so
`primitiveFind` is already the catalogue's file and reusing it would be double duty; skipping is the
only collision-free option. Checked against the framework library names (error, assert, render,
timing, checkpoint, yaml, platform, registry) with no collisions. The rule is not stated in
`_shared/conventions.md` or the blong-handler skill, and changing shared framework docs affects
other realms, so it was left as a todo.

### D-137 — kukum's operations became the library functions, with no operations layer

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · active_

There is no separate `operations/` layer delegating into `orchestrator/kukum/`: the operations ARE
the library functions. Shared plumbing (types, the `descriptorFor` guard, `contextOf`, `baseResult`,
`collectWarnings`, `toResultFile`, `diagnoseFor`, `diagnose`, `methodName`, `describePrimitives`,
`REALM_TEMPLATE_ROOT`, `SHARED_FILES` and `KukumLibContext`) lives in the package-root
`operation.ts`, which cannot live in `orchestrator/kukum/` because every `.ts` in a handler-group
folder is loaded as a handler and a helpers module has nothing for the loader to classify. Each of
the 12 library files reads `this.platform` and `this.registry` and holds the real logic, moved
verbatim from `operations/<name>.ts`. The guards survived the move: `methodName` lives in
`operation.ts`, "Unknown primitive" was folded into `descriptorFor`, and "Unsupported predicate"
became structural because each predicate is its own file and only registered predicates appear in
the generated methods. `libContext.ts` was deleted, its type now living in `operation.ts`. Tests
kept their `operate(...)` call sites and gained a small shim that builds the `library()` factory and
calls it with the `this` the framework seeds, while `libraries.test.ts` still asserts binding
thinness. Verified: lint clean, 490 of 490 tests including the byte-identical fixture and the real
JSON-RPC suite, and CLI output byte-identical to the pre-collapse baseline for `primitive find` and
`instruction find --target=.`.

## Superseded

### D-087 — kukum add and edit report the files they replaced

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · superseded_

`add` and `edit` return a `warnings` array naming any file they replaced, calling out the two shared
ones (`meta/type/schema.ts`, `meta/db/db.ts`) as lossy because they hold every entity in the realm.
Implementing a merge mode was not an option at the time: the framework keys declared object schemas
as `schema[subject][object]`, so it was not obvious that a second file in the `meta/type` group is
additive. The warning text is mode-aware for the same reason the skip logic is, so a hand-written
file left untouched is never reported as replaced.

### D-094 — The kukum end-to-end fixture is reproducible, not idempotent

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · superseded_

It is committed at `core/blong-kukum/test/fixture/e2e-realm/`, where the `fixture/` segment is tap's
own convention for "never run me", which at least stops tap's defaults from discovering it. The
suite generated the same tree into `.kukum-test/regen` and asserted both the file set and the bytes
matched, which locked the templates against drift without depending on `realm add` being re-runnable
in place — it is not.

The generated fixture tree is now gitignored and regenerated in place; the committed Playwright
screenshots are what lock the generators, so the byte-comparison assertion is gone.

Superseded by `D-107`.
